title: Know Your Customer Technical Reference
readerIntent: Understand the optional KYC capability and its high-sensitivity governance requirements.
priorKnowledge: Understand customer identity, workflows, providers, security, audit, and retention.
owner: Optional KYC capability; Profile retains customer identity ownership
summary: KYC coordinates verification cases, evidence references, checks, decisions, provider interactions, and audit without duplicating customer identity or exposing sensitive evidence broadly.

sections.heading: Authority and case model
items: The KYC capability owns cases, requirements, checks, evidence metadata, consent references, decisions, expiry, review, and audit; Profile owns customer identity.
A case binds tenant, customer, purpose, jurisdiction, policy/version, required checks, status, owner, dates, and safe provider references.
Raw documents and biometrics use approved secure storage and access policy; ordinary models, logs, search, events, and frontend state contain only necessary metadata.

sections.heading: Verification lifecycle
items: Open validates identity reference, purpose, consent, jurisdiction, duplicate/active cases, policy, retention, and required checks.
Automatic provider checks and manual reviewer actions may coexist in Workflow, but the KYC service owns final state and target authorization.
Pending, information-required, under-review, approved, rejected, expired, revoked, appealed, and closed transitions carry reason, actor, evidence, revision, and audit.

sections.heading: Provider boundary
items: Adapters receive minimum required data through configured endpoints and secret references, normalize provider status and errors, and never expose vendor SDKs to Profile or clients.
Timeout after submission creates an uncertain check reconciled by provider reference; blind replay may duplicate cost or verification.
Provider selection, residency, supported document types, rate, timeout, retry, circuit, fallback, webhook verification, and data deletion are explicit configuration.

sections.heading: Privacy and security
items: Enforce purpose limitation, consent, encryption, field masking, least privilege, separation of duties, residency, retention, deletion, legal hold, access review, and incident response.
Public responses do not reveal detailed fraud signals, document data, provider payloads, credentials, reviewer notes, or whether another customer's case exists.
Service callbacks authenticate source, bind tenant and case, validate replay and signature, and cannot directly update Profile credentials.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test valid and invalid identity, wrong tenant, missing consent, duplicate case, document boundaries, provider timeout, webhook replay, manual override, appeal, expiry, and revocation.
Test cross-role access, masking, retention/deletion, provider outage, uncertain reconciliation, workflow recovery, audit integrity, migration, load, and regression.
Monitor case age, check latency, provider error, manual backlog, expiry, unresolved uncertainty, access, deletion, and incidents with legal and operational ownership.

sections.heading: Contract
items: Tenant/customer reference, case, requirement, check, provider reference, evidence metadata, consent, decision, expiry, reviewer, status, reason, and audit.
Provider adapters receive minimum required data through governed secrets and endpoints; raw evidence storage and access follow project legal/security policy.
Manual and automatic actions use Workflow where configured; target KYC services own decisions.
Profile remains identity authority and references KYC status through governed contracts rather than copied credentials/evidence.

sections.heading: Production evidence
items: Data minimization, encryption, field masking, purpose/consent, residency, retention/deletion, access review, provider outage, duplicate/replay, manual override, audit integrity, incident response, legal review, performance, and regression tests.
